title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and follow directions, take buses and autos, and tell a driver where to go and where to stop.
intro:
Directions in Telugu are given with commands: *నేరుగా వెళ్ళండి* (go straight), *కుడి వైపు తిరగండి* (turn right). You'll learn the polite and informal **imperative** forms, and the case endings for movement: **-కి** (to), **నుంచి** (from) and **వరకు** (as far as).

In Telugu cities, the auto-rickshaw is king. Notice the typical way to hail one: *చార్మినార్ వస్తారా?* ('Will you come to Charminar?').

vocab.note: To the right: కుడి వైపు (vaipu, side).

vocab.en: up to, until, as far as

phrases.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
Auto! Will you go to Koti?
Does this bus go to Secunderabad?
I'm lost. (lit. I've lost the way)

grammar.title: Commands: polite -ండి and informal
grammar.body:
The **informal** command is the bare verb stem: *రా* (come), *చూడు* (look), *ఆగు* (wait), *వెళ్ళు* (go). Use it with close friends, children and juniors.

The **polite** (and plural) command adds **-ండి** (-ṇḍi), with -u becoming -a: *రండి*, *చూడండి*, *ఆగండి*, *వెళ్ళండి*, *తిరగండి*. This is the safe default with strangers and drivers.

**Don't!**: informal stem + **-కు** (*వెళ్ళకు*, don't go), polite stem + **-కండి** (*వెళ్ళకండి*). The word *వద్దు* can also follow a verbal noun: *వెళ్ళడం వద్దు* (no going).

grammar.title: To, from, as far as, by
grammar.body:
**Destination** takes the dative **-కి / -కు**: స్టేషనుకి (to the station), ఇంటికి (home), హైదరాబాదుకి. Here/there/where become ఇక్కడికి, అక్కడికి, ఎక్కడికి. For going to a person, use **దగ్గరికి**: *డాక్టర్ దగ్గరికి*.

**Source**: **నుంచి** (from): *ఇక్కడి నుంచి* (from here; note ఇక్కడ → ఇక్కడి). **Limit**: **వరకు** (up to): *స్టేషను వరకు*.

**Means of transport** uses **-లో** (in): *బస్సులో*, *రైల్లో*, *ఆటోలో*. On foot is *నడిచి* ('having walked').

examples.native: స్టేషను నుంచి ఇంటి వరకు ఆటోలో వచ్చాను.
examples.roman: sṭēṣanu nunchi iṇṭi varaku āṭōlō vachchānu.
examples.en: I came from the station to the house by auto.
Tomorrow I'll go to Vijayawada by train.
How far is it from here?

dialogue.title: To Charminar
dialogue.setting: A visitor asks a passer-by the way to Charminar in Hyderabad, then takes an auto.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.en: Excuse me, how do I get to Charminar?

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.native: ఇక్కడి నుంచి కొంచెం దూరం. ఆటోలో వెళ్ళండి.
lines.roman: ikkaḍi nunchi konchem dūram. āṭōlō veḷḷaṇḍi.
lines.en: It's a bit far from here. Take an auto.

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.native: వెళ్ళొచ్చు, కానీ అరగంట పడుతుంది. ఈ రోడ్డులో నేరుగా వెళ్ళి, సిగ్నల్ దగ్గర ఎడమ వైపు తిరగండి.
lines.roman: veḷḷochchu, kānī aragaṇṭa paḍutundi. ī rōḍḍulō nērugā veḷḷi, signal daggara eḍama vaipu tiragaṇḍi.
lines.en: You can, but it takes half an hour. Go straight down this road and turn left at the signal.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.en: Thank you. Auto! Will you go to Charminar?

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.en: That much? Put the meter on.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.en: Stop here, please. How much is it?

culture: Directions in Telugu towns are given by **landmarks** rather than street names: 'past the temple, opposite the bank, next to the big tamarind tree'. Many neighbourhood names end in *-పేట* (pēṭa, town), *-పల్లి* (palli, village), *-గూడ* (gūḍa) or *-నగర్* (nagar). Auto drivers often quote a fixed fare; asking for the meter, or using a ride-hailing app, is normal.

tip.title: To and from: -కి and నుంచి
tip.body:
- Where you're going takes **-కి / -కు**: గుడి**కి**, బ్యాంకు**కి**, ఇంటి**కి**.
- Here / there / where become **ఇక్కడికి, అక్కడికి, ఎక్కడికి** (to here, to there, where to?).
- Where you start from takes **నుంచి**: ఇక్కడ → **ఇక్కడి నుంచి** 'from here'.
- How do I get to…? = place**కి ఎలా వెళ్ళాలి?**

sentences.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the temple?
Where are you going?
I'm going to the market.
I'll go to the bank tomorrow.
Does this way go to the station?
How far is the temple from here?
Let's walk to the market.
The station is very far from here.
The temple isn't far, you can walk.
Sorry, I'm new here too.

tip.title: Commands: polite -ండి, informal bare stem
tip.body:
- To a stranger or a driver add **-ండి** (final -u → -a): తిరుగు → **తిరగండి**, వెళ్ళు → **వెళ్ళండి**, చూడు → **చూడండి**.
- To a friend or a child just use the bare stem: **తిరుగు**, **వెళ్ళు**, **చూడు**.
- Side = **వైపు**: కుడి వైపు 'to the right', ఎడమ వైపు 'to the left'.

sentences.native: నేరుగా వెళ్ళండి, తర్వాత కుడి వైపు తిరగండి.
sentences.roman: nērugā veḷḷaṇḍi, tarvāta kuḍi vaipu tiragaṇḍi.
sentences.en: Go straight on, then turn right.
Turn left at the first turning.

sentences.native: ఎడమ వైపు కాదు, కుడి వైపు తిరుగు!
sentences.roman: eḍama vaipu kādu, kuḍi vaipu tirugu!
sentences.en: Not left, turn right! (to a friend)
Go straight down this lane. (to a friend)
Look to the right at the corner.
Go slowly, there's a bend here.
Come over here, please.
To the right or to the left?
Our house is in the third lane.

tip.title: Directions by landmark
tip.body:
- People give directions by landmarks, not street names: బ్యాంకు **ఎదురుగా** 'opposite the bank', గుడి **పక్కన** 'next to the temple', కూడలి **దగ్గర** 'at the junction'.
- **వరకు** 'up to, as far as' follows the place: వంతెన **వరకు** నేరుగా వెళ్ళండి.
- Lost? Say **నేను దారి తప్పిపోయాను**.

sentences.en: The temple is opposite the market.

sentences.native: ఈ రోడ్డులో వంతెన వరకు నేరుగా వెళ్ళండి.
sentences.roman: ī rōḍḍulō vantena varaku nērugā veḷḷaṇḍi.
sentences.en: Go straight along this road as far as the bridge.
Turn left at the junction.
How far is it to the station?
Our office is opposite the bank.

sentences.native: కూడలి నుంచి గుడి వరకు నడిచి వెళ్ళండి.
sentences.roman: kūḍali nunchi guḍi varaku naḍichi veḷḷaṇḍi.
sentences.en: Walk from the junction to the temple.
Turn right after the bridge.

sentences.native: బ్యాంకు ఈ వీధిలో లేదు, పక్క వీధిలో ఉంది.
sentences.roman: byāṅku ī vīdhilō lēdu, pakka vīdhilō undi.
sentences.en: The bank isn't on this street, it's on the next one.
What's the name of this street?

tip.title: Stop, wait and don't
tip.body:
- **ఆగండి** 'wait, stop (yourself)'; **ఆపండి** 'stop it' (the auto, the car): ఇక్కడ ఆపండి.
- Don't! Polite: stem + **-కండి**: ఆపకండి, వెళ్ళకండి. Informal: stem + **-కు**: ఆగకు, వెళ్ళకు.
- Hail an auto with the place + **వస్తారా?** 'will you come?'

sentences.en: Wait a minute, please.
Stop at the temple, please.
Don't stop here, stop at the bank.
Don't go into that lane, please.
Don't stop in the road. (to a friend)
Go slowly, there's no hurry.
Auto! Will you go to the station?
How long does it take to the market?
How much is on the meter?

tip.title: By bus, by train: -లో
tip.body:
- The vehicle takes **-లో** 'in': బస్సు**లో**, కారు**లో**, ఆటో**లో**; రైలు → **రైల్లో**.
- A scooter or bike is ridden *on*: బండి **మీద**.
- Get on = **ఎక్కు** (ఎక్కండి), get off = **దిగు** (దిగండి): బస్సు ఎక్కండి, ఇక్కడ దిగండి.

sentences.en: I go to the office by bus every day.
Shall we go by train or by bus?
I'll go to the airport by car.
My brother comes on his scooter.
Get on the bus here.
Get off at the bus station.
Where are you getting off? (to a friend)
This bus goes as far as the bus station.
Two tickets, please.
What time does the train come?
We don't have a car.
